program: Integrated housing, recuperative care and supportive health services

what: Illumination Health + Home, formerly Illumination Foundation, combines housing with recuperative care and supportive services.
The conditional estimate prices a substantial medical-respite component against the full recipient budget.
Housing, family services and other health pathways remain unpriced, so this is not a complete portfolio ranking.
strengths: Post-hospital recuperative care has a concrete clinical mechanism and external randomized evidence.
Current reported respite volume anchors scale without treating all clients as marginal beneficiaries.
The cost reconstruction includes recognized donated resources and separately netted event costs.
reservations: External randomized QALY differences were small and statistically uncertain.
CalAIM, hospital payments and public contracts can substitute for donations.
LA/Orange residence and current marginal capacity are unmeasured; Inland Empire activity is outside the edition.

sections.what: The [current organization](https://illuminationhealthhome.org/) confirms the name change from Illumination Foundation. The same EIN, 71-1047686, is the recipient; housing and integrated services are included rather than treating respite as a separately restricted charity. [Healthcare services](https://illuminationhealthhome.org/service/healthcare-services/) include post-hospital recovery and behavioral support. The older [service overview](https://www.ifhomeless.org/) describes Orange County, Los Angeles County and Inland Empire operations. Riverside and San Bernardino benefits are outside this LA–Orange MSA; headquarters is not beneficiary geography.
sections.monitoring: The [FY2024–25 impact report](https://illuminationhealthhome.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Illumination_2024-25_Impact-Report.pdf) reports 2,329 recuperative-care clients, 6,826 clients overall and 1,719 housed. These are outputs, not additional health gains, and categories can overlap. The model uses respite volume only, with no extra housing QALYs added for the same clients. Track unique admissions, comparable discharge alternatives, symptom and EQ-5D trajectories, completion, readmission and resident county. The latest throughput is paired with FY2024 audited cost as a prospective scale approximation, not a matched-year observed cost per outcome.
sections.qualitative:
A [Danish randomized respite study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12913-020-05358-4) compared a two-week recovery stay with usual discharge arrangements. It found lower subsequent costs, but the between-group QALY difference was small and not statistically significant. The first six participants were assigned to intervention rather than randomized, and quality-of-life follow-up was incomplete. Different insurance, housing and clinical needs limit transfer. Hospital savings are not QALYs, and a negative cost-utility ratio does not establish a large health effect.

The central q=0.005 QALY is an explicit modest health-area judgment per otherwise additional respite episode, not the trial's measured coefficient. It represents about 1.8 quality-adjusted days over no more than one year. Zero or adverse health is possible. No avoided-death lifetime term, housing effect, or repeated annual cohort is added.
sections.cost:
The retained partial clinical reference is $493,749,768.83 per ten LA clinical QALYs at $55,822,486 full recipient annual cost. Signed household resources have been assessed but remain unknown; this is not a numerical income recalibration, a complete portfolio estimate, or an empirical 90% health finding.

The [FY2024–25 impact report](https://illuminationhealthhome.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Illumination_2024-25_Impact-Report.pdf) establishes respite, housing and navigation activity, but their overlapping client counts cannot be added or converted automatically into unique households. A client story records SNAP and general-relief access with Social Security still pursued; it supplies no annual retained award amount. Housing and healthcare can change actual rent, food, private payments and access costs, but the current sources do not identify net household amounts against existing shelter, CalAIM, hospital and alternative-provider arrangements. A conditional model needs that operational payment/cohort bridge, not necessarily an RCT.

Resources must be jointly assessed within households: taxes, withdrawn benefits, rent, commuting and full time/opportunity costs may offset benefits independently of clinical response. Positive health/housing overlap would limit gains only, never erase incurred costs. Lower hospital spending is a payer outcome, not patient disposable income; public finance and landlord incidence remain separate. No retail housing/care value or ordinary survivor earnings is credited. Employment assistance, family supports and the broader portfolio remain unquantified. The income-unknown world preserves the clinical reference while leaving combined welfare unpriced.

FY2024 gross recognized recipient cost is $55,822,486: $55,426,178 audited expense plus $396,308 netted event costs. The audit includes donated services/materials/facilities and depreciation. [Original audit](https://illuminationhealthhome.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/The-Illumination-Foundation-06.30.2024.pdf) The FY2023 original return reconciles $47,541,549 to $47,992,708 audited expense through $451,159 donated services/facilities; adding $321,001 event costs gives $48,313,709. FY2022 return expense plus events is $39,155,013, but its donated-resource reconciliation is not verified, so that year is noncomparable and no synthetic three-year mean is supplied.

At full recipient cost, 2,329 respite clients × 0.5 net service additionality × 0.25 funding responsiveness × 0.005 QALY × 0.8 LA/Orange share / 1.03 gives 1.130583 LA QALYs, or $493.75 million per 10. These fractions are judgments, not observed conversion rates. The wide positive cases, zero and adverse stress retain uncertainty. Outside hospital, clinical and partner resources require separate societal costing; savings are not subtracted from this recipient denominator.
sections.funding: The [FY2024 audit](https://illuminationhealthhome.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/The-Illumination-Foundation-06.30.2024.pdf) reports $35.90m program fees and $16.23m federal/state contracts and grants. Net assets were $22.93m, including $1.27m restricted, but much of the balance sheet is property rather than spendable cash. These figures do not prove a current funding gap. CalAIM and hospital alternatives make funding response distinct from clinical effectiveness. The [current impact report](https://illuminationhealthhome.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Illumination_2024-25_Impact-Report.pdf) identifies CalOptima partnership; financed expansion is baseline, not automatically caused by a new gift.

model.costScope: Full recognized recipient annual cost; respite-health component only, not complete portfolio or social-resource return. The full annual budget is a ratio normalization, not a requested donation or verified funding tranche. Applying the ratio to an ordinary small gift assumes locally proportional capacity response and the stated component allocation.
model.geographicAttribution: g=.8 subjective LA/Orange resident share, sensitivity .5–.95; Inland Empire excluded.
model.formula: Qall=2329*a*b*q/1.03; QLA=Qall*g; price10=10*55822486/QLA. q is finite total health area, not annual recurring utility.
model.counterfactual: Existing hospital discharge, public contracts, CalAIM, other respite providers and donor replacement continue. a adjusts service substitution; b adjusts capacity response to ordinary funds once.
model.attribution: No additional coalition multiplier. No repeat respite or overlapping housing QALYs credited; verify unique clients.
model.uncertainty: Explicit subjective central; trial is counterevidence to large health claims. Latest throughput and prior-year cost require updating.
model.nativeOutcomes: Central 2329*.5*.25=291.125 expected additional respite episodes before geography, not observed marginal patients.

inputs.name: a
inputs.rationale: Alternative publicly financed respite and discharge care; test .2–.9.

inputs.name: q
inputs.rationale: No more than one year; test .0005–.03 plus zero/harm; not observed RCT coefficient. Treat this as expected net first-year health area, inclusive of competing mortality, intervention burden and benefit fade within the year; it is not a utility level maintained for every survivor.

scenarios.label: central
scenarios.assumptions: N=2329; a=0.5; b=0.25; q=0.005 finite QALYs per otherwise additional respite episode; g=0.8; one year maximum, 3% discount. Subjective joint case, not confidence bounds.

scenarios.label: low
scenarios.assumptions: N=2329; a=0.2; b=0.05; q=0.0005 finite QALYs per otherwise additional respite episode; g=0.5; one year maximum, 3% discount. Subjective joint case, not confidence bounds.

scenarios.label: high
scenarios.assumptions: N=2329; a=0.9; b=0.75; q=0.03 finite QALYs per otherwise additional respite episode; g=0.95; one year maximum, 3% discount. Subjective joint case, not confidence bounds.

scenarios.label: zero
scenarios.assumptions: No additional benefit or full substitution.

scenarios.label: adverse
scenarios.assumptions: Illustrative one LA QALY net harm, not observed. This direct one-year local-harm stress assumes g=1 for the harmed population; it is not derived using the central geography fraction.

scenarios.label: Combined household resources unknown; clinical reference retained
scenarios.assumptions: Original partial clinical reference is unchanged. This null combined diagnostic does not infer zero income or withdraw clinical arithmetic.

sensitivity: Halving q or b doubles price.

incomeAssessment.scope: Targeted household payments, benefits and housing resources; original clinical estimate is a partial reference, not complete portfolio value.
incomeAssessment.rationale: Reported respite and housing clients establish activity, and the benefits vignette establishes a resource mechanism. Neither supplies a current unique household/payment cohort or retained dollar amount. Hospital savings are payer outcomes, not disposable client resources.
directions: Additional retained SNAP/general relief or disability benefits may raise consumption; taxes and other benefits withdrawn must be netted.
Housing may replace actual rent or increase rent and food obligations relative to shelter or institutional alternatives.
Medical private payments, travel, time and opportunity costs require actual alternative coverage and discharge arrangements; full burdens are independent of clinical response.
Employment assistance and family supports remain unquantified; no gross wages or retail housing/care value is credited.

priceScope: Working judgment price for the recuperative-care health component, charging full recorded recipient cost. Other portfolio effects and unrecognized external resource costs remain unestimated; this is not a measured whole-portfolio or societal return.
